**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

if the difference is between cx_oracle 6.0.1 and 6.0.3, minor bugfix releases, then this is most certainly a regression on the cx_Oracle side and it should be reported there first.    There's then again the chance we have to do setinputsizes() on this end but please post a case at https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/issues

**Leonid Butenko wrote:**

Did it already: https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/issues/184

I have also found some old thread saying that the support of NaNs was explicitly disabled in cx_Oralce starting from 6.0.3 as long as it corrupts the data. https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/issues/91. What are the alternatives then? We've been using NaNs for ages and have never experienced any kind of data corruption.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

that's weird because oracle say's it's supported: https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E11882_01/server.112/e41084/sql_elements001.htm#SQLRF50979   so Anthony needs to clarify.

I've also never heard of Oracle being used in science, I've only seen it in finance and otherwise very front-facing big businesses.     too expensive for scientific budgets and also doesn't offer any particular kind of value over the more common choice (e.g. Postgresql).

**Leonid Butenko wrote:**

The key point in choosing Oracle for our organisation is the ability to handle big amount of data (many terabytes) as long as we process live data from meteorological satellites. Another important point is 24/7 support.

```
import sqlalchemy as sa
import sqlalchemy.orm
import datetime
import sqlalchemy.ext.declarative

connection_string = "oracle://scott:tiger@oracle1120/"

engine = sa.create_engine(connection_string, echo = True, max_overflow = 0, pool_size = 3)
_session = sa.orm.sessionmaker()
_session.configure(bind=engine)
session = _session()

class BinaryFloat(sqlalchemy.types.TypeDecorator):

    impl = sqlalchemy.types.Numeric

    def load_dialect_impl(self, dialect):
        if dialect.name == 'oracle':
            return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.dialects.oracle.BINARY_FLOAT)
        else:
            return dialect.type_descriptor(sqlalchemy.types.FLOAT(23)) # < 24 bit mantissa is a single precision number

table = sa.Table(
    "nan_test", sa.MetaData(),
    sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
    sa.Column("fval", BinaryFloat )
)
table.drop(engine)
table.create(engine, checkfirst=True)

Base = sa.ext.declarative.declarative_base()

class Pod(Base):
    __table__ = sa.Table(
        "nan_test", Base.metadata, autoload = True, autoload_with = engine)

session.add(Pod(id=1, fval=float('nan')))
session.commit()

```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

it's a little confusing to explain how this is failing.  there are two fixes I can make both of which will resolve the above test script but differently.


first off, usually, if you have a special TypeDecorator, that implies you want there to be some special in-Python behaviors for it, which means you'd want to make sure that is specified when you reflect:

```
class Pod(Base):
    __table__ = sa.Table(
        "nan_test", Base.metadata,

        sa.Column("fval", BinaryFloat ),

        autoload = True, autoload_with = engine)

```


however, this is still not resolving your case, since the thing I'm doing for #4264 as well as the previous issue in this regard is not taking TypeDecorators into account.    That is the the first thing I have to fix.

Next, you really don't need to be using a TypeDecorator here, you should use a Variant (which is itself a TypeDecorator designed for this purpose):

    BinaryFloat = sqlalchemy.types.Numeric().with_variant(sa.dialects.oracle.BINARY_FLOAT(), "oracle") 

That still needs me to do the same fix since this is still a TypeDecorator.

But next, to confuse the whole matter entirely, you are reflecting the table, so that should be giving you the correct Oracle datatype in any case, and then you *dont* need to override the column, and it will all work.  But!  that is *also* not working since this type needs to be added to a list, right now you see:

/opt/mettools/envs/py27/lib/python2.7/site-packages/SQLAlchemy-1.3.0b1.dev0-py2.7-linux-x86_64.egg/sqlalchemy/dialects/oracle/base.py:1410: SAWarning: Did not recognize type 'BINARY_FLOAT' of column 'fval'


so there are two issues to fix and test.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Turn oracle BINARY_DOUBLE, BINARY_FLOAT, DOUBLE_PRECISION into floats

The Oracle BINARY_FLOAT and BINARY_DOUBLE datatypes now participate within
cx_Oracle.setinputsizes(), passing along NATIVE_FLOAT, so as to support the
NaN value.  Additionally, :class:`.oracle.BINARY_FLOAT`,
:class:`.oracle.BINARY_DOUBLE` and :class:`.oracle.DOUBLE_PRECISION` now
subclass :class:`.Float`, since these are floating point datatypes, not
decimal.  These datatypes were already defaulting the
:paramref:`.Float.asdecimal` flag to False in line with what
:class:`.Float` already does.

Added reflection capabilities for the :class:`.oracle.BINARY_FLOAT`,
:class:`.oracle.BINARY_DOUBLE` datatypes.

Change-Id: Id99b912e83052654a17d07dc92b4dcb958cb7600
Fixes: #4264
